tagline: A farm loop out of a town once called 79.
intro: The loop starts among the early-1900s railroad depots of downtown Millen and heads out on State Route 23 and Perkins Green Fork Road, past woodland, pasture and old farmhouses in small scattered communities. Herndon Road brings a few historic churches. State Route 17 comes home across open farmland that runs on for miles.
Millen was settled in 1835 under the name "79", its rough distance in miles from Savannah. When two railroads met here in 1854 it took the name of a railway superintendent instead.

moments.title: Downtown Millen
moments.text: The railroad depots downtown date from the early 1900s, long after Sherman's march came through on December 3, 1864, and Union soldiers destroyed the junction.

moments.title: Camp Lawton at Magnolia Springs
moments.text: Springs running some 7 million gallons a day drew a Confederate prison stockade here in 1864, and it held over 10,000 Union soldiers for barely six weeks before Sherman's advance emptied it.
